 --> Petrol, diesel prices won't come down immediately, says Suresh Gopi; here's why
 Petrol, diesel prices: Suresh Gopi says immediate cuts are not possible due to Rs 42,000 crore in oil company losses and supply disruptions. 
 Moneycontrol News 
 November 16, 2026 / 07:45 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Union Minister Suresh Gopi says an immediate petrol and diesel price cut is not feasible, citing Rs 42,000 crore in oil company losses and disruptions in petroleum supplies. Fuel price cut not feasible due to oil firm losses.
 Companies face Rs 42,000 crore losses from West Asia crisis.
 States can reduce local taxes on petrol and diesel.

 Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi on Monday said an immediate reduction in petrol and diesel prices was not feasible, citing Rs 42,000 crore in losses incurred by oil companies amid the West Asia conflict and disruptions in petroleum supplies, news agency ANI reported. 
 Speaking to reporters at Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, Gopi said oil companies would first have to account for their accumulated losses before reducing fuel prices. 
 "We may wish for prices to come down the next day. But technically it is not possible right away," he said. 
 Gopi did not specify the period covered by the Rs 42,000 crore loss figure. 
 The minister said individual states could reduce taxes on petrol. He referred to price increases in Kerala and Karnataka, while saying he was unaware of the extent of changes in Tamil Nadu. 
 Gopi also acknowledged disruptions in petroleum supplies and said the government was taking steps to resolve them. 
 "There is chaos in the supply of petroleum products. We are doing whatever needs to be done to fix it," he said. 
 Government's earlier measures on fuel prices 
 The remarks follow a series of government interventions aimed at managing fuel prices and supplies during the West Asia conflict. 
 On March 27, the Centre reduced excise duty on petrol and diesel by Rs 10 per litre each following a sharp increase in international crude prices. 
 The Petroleum Ministry said the reduction was intended to offset part of the losses incurred by public sector oil marketing companies rather than lower retail prices. The companies include Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation. 
 In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on July 30, Gopi said petrol and diesel prices were market-determined, with public sector oil companies responsible for pricing decisions. 
 He told Parliament that India's crude oil basket had risen from $69 per barrel in February to $136.68 in March, before standing at $103.33 on July 23. Oil companies had increased retail prices only marginally despite incurring losses, he said. 
 The government had also imposed temporary restrictions on diesel purchases at retail outlets from June 12, limiting sales to 200 litres per customer or vehicle per day to address diversion, hoarding and black marketing. The restrictions were withdrawn from July 1 following a review of supplies. 
 Retail fuel prices also vary across states because of differences in VAT and sales tax rates, which are determined by state governments. 
 Karnataka minister raises ethanol procurement concerns 
 Separately, on November 8, Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil accused the Centre of encouraging higher ethanol production without ensuring adequate procurement. 
 Speaking in Bengaluru, Patil alleged that the Union Government was refusing to procure even 20-30 per cent of ethanol output despite previously promoting blending targets including E10, E20 and E30. 
 He also called for an investigation into alleged irregularities in the ethanol blending process, according to ANI.
